title: SharePoint agents: who can use them, what they can read and how they are billed
summary: Hold: the licensing control starts inside a details page rather than giving the route from the admin center, and its automation is incorrectly reported as undocumented. Most other claims are supported, but Microsoft pages disagree about some billing requirements and the audit-collection command; those differences need to be acknowledged.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents answer questions and provide insights from SharePoint sites, pages and document libraries.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint, powered by AI, help users quickly find information and insights on SharePoint sites, pages, and document libraries.

claims.where: Governance controls: How they interact; Why it matters
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery keeps a site's content out of Copilot and organisation-wide search.
claims.quote: The restricted content discovery policy leaves site access unchanged but prevents the site's content from being surfaced in Microsoft Copilot or organization-wide search for all users.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket exclusion and the suggestion that this limits all agent reading with 'Restricted Content Discovery limits tenant-wide discovery of the site's content and removes AI entry points; it does not change permissions or stop Copilot from summarizing an already-open document.' The cited access page gives a broader description, whereas https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery explicitly excludes experiences operating on content already in use; cite that qualification.

claims.claim: The admin-center route to the per-user service-plan toggle is License details page for Microsoft Copilot > Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. ... On the Licenses page, select the row for a specific user or group you want to change. ... In the details pane, select or deselect the apps and services
claims.fix: Replace the part-way-in route with 'Billing > Licenses > user or group > Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint'. Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint for the service-plan label and add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users for the navigation to the user or group details pane.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation to enable or disable the user's Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint service plan.
claims.quote: You can also enable and disable specific plans associated with a subscription. ... You can disable servicePlans associated with a license by setting the disabledPlans property on an assignedLicense object.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api null with kind 'graph', call 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-assignlicense?view=graph-rest-1.0'. Add to its note: 'Set addLicenses[].skuId to the Copilot SKU and addLicenses[].disabledPlans to the service-plan IDs to disable, preserving any already-disabled plans; removeLicenses is required and may be empty.' https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/enterprise/disable-access-to-services-with-microsoft-365-powershell explains preserving existing disabled plans.

claims.claim: The SharePoint agent billing connection is at Copilot > Billing and usage > Pay-as-you-go services > SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Copilot > Billing and usage. ... Choose SharePoint agents from the list of apps and services. The Manage billing policy connections pane appears.
claims.fix: Complete the existing route as 'Copilot > Billing and usage > Pay-as-you-go services > SharePoint agents > billing policy', with a note that the policy is selected in Manage billing policy connections. Also note that https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot documents the alternative entry 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage' and a Connection status toggle set to Connected; retain the SharePoint-specific route as the cited page's route rather than silently choosing between the pages.

claims.claim: No documented command or API was found to create or connect the Microsoft 365 billing policy specifically for SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents pay as you go billing policy create connect API PowerShell; "SharePoint agents" "billing policy" "API" "create". Read sharepoint-agents-azure-billing, copilot/implement/setup-pay-as-you-go and the Copilot-node setup guide; results gave no feature-specific operation.

claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. ... Select the site you want to configure. ... Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for the site.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: Reports > Agent Insights in the SharePoint admin center reaches reporting on agents across SharePoint and OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, expand Reports and then select Agent Insights. ... As a SharePoint Administrator, select Create a report to create the report.
claims.fix: Complete the route for generating the report as 'Reports > Agent Insights > Create a report > Report duration'. The cited page says to enter a name and specify the time frame under Report duration, then select Create and run.

claims.claim: Start-SPOCopilotAgentInsightsReport -ReportPeriodInDays <28> generates an Agent Insights report for the past 28 days.
claims.quote: For example, to generate a report for the past 28 days, run the command: ... Start-SPOCopilotAgentInsightsReport -ReportPeriodInDays <28>

claims.claim: No admin UI control was found for enabling the audit-data collection that feeds Agent Insights.
claims.quote: Searched: Start-SPOAuditDataCollectionForActivityInsights enable data collection admin center UI; site:learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint "Agent Insights" "data collection" "enable". Read insights-on-sharepoint-agents and the cmdlet reference; they document PowerShell, not a UI control.

claims.claim: Start-SPOAuditDataCollectionForActivityInsights enables collection for the agent report.
claims.quote: This PowerShell command starts collecting audit data for reports on activities from the last 28 days. ... Start-SPOAuditDataCollectionForActivityInsights
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'Start-SPOAuditDataCollectionForActivityInsights -ReportEntity CopilotAppInsights' and point its docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/start-spoauditdatacollectionforactivityinsights?view=sharepoint-ps. Note the documentation discrepancy: the SharePoint overview omits ReportEntity, while the cmdlet reference makes it mandatory, lists CopilotAppInsights and labels the Copilot-agent scenario Private Preview.

claims.claim: Reports can be generated 24 hours after audit-data collection is enabled.
claims.quote: After you enable data collection, you can generate the reports after 24 hours.

claims.claim: Without a SharePoint Advanced Management licence, audit-data collection must be enabled for Agent Insights.
claims.quote: If you don't have a Microsoft SharePoint Advanced Management license, you need to enable data collection.
